title: Redwood Discovery - Lynx Fintech - Latency & Throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency and streaming behavior across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; agreed to run token/sec and p95 benchmarks and follow up with security docs and pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Samir to send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing and perf matrix by 2026-06-01
Jenna to share benchmark script and run with Lynx prompt set; deliver results by 2026-06-04
Schedule Private deployment security review with Security PM (optionally SAML/SOC2 deep dive) w/in 2 weeks
action_items: Samir Patel: Send pricing + SLA doc by 2026-06-01
Jenna Ortiz: Run latency token/sec benchmark with 8k context and share results by 2026-06-04
Priya Kapoor (Lynx): Provide 200 sample prompts and p95 target definitions by 2026-05-31
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-28 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55 min | Attendees: Samir, Jenna (Redwood); Maya, Carlos, Priya, Devon (Lynx)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. Jenna is our solutions engineer, she'll cover the deep perf stuff. Quick run of agenda - p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and then next steps for benchmarks.

[00:22] Maya: Hi Samir, thanks. We are evaluating Hosted first but open to Dedicated or Private if latency/concurrency or compliance needs push us there. Our SLO is p95 under 250 ms for single-turn generation at 256 tokens, and we expect peaks of ~200 concurrency for customer-facing inference.

[00:45] Jenna: Okay great, thanks. Just to clarify, that 250ms p95 - is that end-to-end including network from our app, or pure model generation on the inference side?

[01:01] Maya: We mean user-perceived, so includes call time. But we're happy to start by understanding raw model inference p95 so we can budget network and app latencies.

[01:20] Samir: Totally. Quick call out: Hosted typical raw inference p95 for mid-sized open models is in the 200-600ms range depending on sequence length and stream vs non-stream. Dedicated often improves raw p95 by ~30-60% since you get reserved GPU pools. But of course numbers vary with model and quantization.

[01:48] Carlos: When you say streaming vs non-streaming, what's the delta? We're doing streaming token-by-token to reduce first-byte latency.

[02:00] Jenna: Streaming helps perceived latency - first token can be delivered much earlier. For token-per-second throughput, it depends on model; streaming doesn't change total tokens/sec that a GPU can do, but it changes tail latency, especially p95 of first-byte. Example: for a 1B-7B family model, we might see first byte p95 ~80-150ms on Dedicated and 150-300ms on Hosted, with sustained token/sec of ~200-800 depending on context length and quantization.

[02:35] Priya: Those token/sec numbers seem low vs what we expect. Our ops folks have benchmarked ~1.5k tokens/sec on our internal cluster for optimized kernels. Is that comparable?

[02:47] Jenna: Yeah, it can be higher - on high-end GPUs and with aggressive quantization and compilation you can reach >1k tokens/sec. I was giving conservative ranges for mixed loads. We'll run your actual prompt set to get precise numbers.

[03:05] Devon: Pause - our traffic is very spiky, we need to handle bursts to 400 concurrent requests for short windows. How does Redwood handle that - autoscale or burst pools?

[03:18] Samir: For Dedicated we support reserved capacity plus burst capacity options, and routing policies to fallback to hosted or lower-cost variants if needed. For Hosted we have regional routing and soft limits - but if you need strict latency SLOs at scale, Dedicated or Private is recommended.

[03:40] Maya: What's the multi-tenant noise impact on Hosted p95?

[03:45] Jenna: We do per-tenant queues, but yes, noisy neighbor effects exist. Hosted is multitenant; we mitigate via scheduling and continuous batching heuristics, and we publish model performance profiles. If your p95 target is strict, Dedicated gives isolation.

[04:02] Carlos: On Private - we have strict data residency and KMS requirements. Does Redwood Private support customer-managed KMS and SOC2/ISO audit logs?

[04:13] Samir: Yes - Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. We also have a SOC 2 report available and SSO/SAML for RBAC. We can set up a security review.

[04:30] Priya: For benchmarking: what inputs do you need? We can provide 200 sample prompts across short and long contexts, and specify p95 targets per route.

[04:42] Jenna: Perfect. We'll need: prompt set, typical concurrency pattern (poisson or spikes), expected token output distributions, and whether you use streaming or single response. We'll run token/sec and p95 runs across Hosted (representative) and a Dedicated-like reserved environment. We'll also share scripts.

[05:05] Maya: Also interested in cost - how to map tokens/sec and concurrency into expected monthly cost for Hosted vs Dedicated.

[05:12] Samir: We'll include cost modeling in the matrix. Dedicated typically reduces unit cost by 30-60% for high sustained throughput. There are commit tiers. Hosted is easiest to start.

[05:30] Carlos: A technical question: how do you handle KV cache across sessions for chat? We do a lot of long-context chat and want fast cache reads.

[05:40] Jenna: Our runtime does KV cache sharing and prefix caching for repeated context; on Dedicated we can pin caches to GPU with low-latency memory access. In some transcriptions our product name is misheard as "Red wood cache" ha, but it's KV cache.

[05:55] Priya: Any quantization options?

[06:02] Jenna: Yes, we support multiple quantization profiles. 4-bit can reduce memory and increase throughput but may impact quality. We'll recommend profiles by model and run quality regression checks against your eval set.

[06:20] Maya: Let's talk p95 numbers for streaming first-byte and full-response. Our main SLO is p95 first-byte <= 120 ms and p95 full-response <= 300 ms for 128-token outputs. Are those realistic?

[06:34] Jenna: For 128 tokens, p95 full-response at 300 ms is aggressive but possible on Dedicated with optimized kernels and shorter context. For Hosted, full-response p95 of 300ms is unlikely for many open models - Hosted might be 400-900ms. First-byte 120ms p95 is achievable on Dedicated with warm caches and streaming. We'll need to benchmark with your prompts.

[07:00] Samir: Action: Jenna will put together a benchmark plan - we typically run cold/hot cache, streaming vs non, variable concurrency (1, 50, 200, 400), and token/sec saturation tests. We'll include raw p95 numbers and user-perceived estimates.

[07:18] Carlos: When you do concurrency tests, do you simulate network and app-side overhead?

[07:25] Jenna: We try to emulate realistic client behavior but we focus on raw model-side numbers; we can add a client latency model to approximate end-to-end. We'll annotate which numbers include network.

[07:38] Maya: For Dedicated, what's the SLA on latency?

[07:43] Samir: We have SLA guarantees on uptime and throughput for Reserved capacity; latency guarantees are more nuanced - we provide target p95 ranges per model and commit tier, and we have escalation windows. We'll include details in the SLA doc.

[07:58] Priya: Can you run benchmarks with 8k context? We have a few flows with long histories up to 8k.

[08:06] Jenna: Yes, we'll run at 2k, 4k, and 8k. Expect token/sec to drop with longer context due to attention work; p95 will increase. We'll record both token/sec and p95 per model and quant profile.

[08:25] Devon: How do you handle failover if Dedicated capacity is saturated? Can you fallback to Hosted or a lower-quality model?

[08:33] Samir: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or Hosted region. You can configure policy: prefer Dedicated but overflow to Hosted or cheaper model for non-critical routes.

[08:48] Carlos: About benchmarks - we need reproducibility. Do you provide the script and seed, and can we run locally in our infra?

[08:55] Jenna: We'll share the benchmark harness (link in notes) and it's runnable on-prem or in cloud. It records timestamps every token and computes p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and full-response, plus tokens/sec. We'll also run an internal run so you get a side-by-side.

[09:12] Maya: Please include throughput vs latency curves - we want to know at what concurrency p95 degrades past our SLOs.

[09:18] Jenna: Absolutely - saturation curves are a core output. We'll show per-model curves and also per-quantization profile.

[09:28] Priya: For private deployment, what's the operations footprint - do we need to manage autoscaling?

[09:34] Samir: Private can be deployed with our control plane on your VPC; we support an ops mode where Redwood manages autoscaling and one where your SREs control it. We provide operator docs and runbooks.

[09:48] Carlos: Security specifics: do you provide SOC2 Type II, ISO, and do you support SAML-based SSO for admin console?

[09:55] Samir: Yes on SOC2. SAML SSO is supported for RBAC on Console. We'll share the compliance pack.

[10:05] Maya: Ok, let's talk sample numbers - if we aim for p95 full-response <= 300ms for 128 tokens, what concurrency on Dedicated is realistic?

[10:15] Jenna: Ballpark: on a reserved pool sized for your workload with optimized model we might hit that at 50-150 concurrent inferences depending on if requests are streaming and average output tokens. But exact number varies; that's why we need to run your set.

[10:30] Priya: Could you run a quick example in this call? Maybe a micro benchmark?

[10:34] Jenna: We don't have a live Dedicated cluster to spin up right now, but I can show a hosted sample run we've got in the deck. (brief link shared) Example: hosted run with model X, 256 context, first-byte p95 220ms, full-response p95 780ms at 20 concurrent.

[11:00] Samir: Note: those hosted numbers are noisy. For your spikes to 400 concurrent, Hosted will likely fall short for strict p95 unless we provision bursts; Dedicated + burst pool or Private is the path for that SLO.

[11:14] Carlos: How do you measure p95 - is it server-side sampling or full histogram?

[11:19] Jenna: We collect full histograms and compute p50/p95/p99 from request logs; we also output per-token timing if you want. The Console shows token-level breakdown.

[11:30] Maya: For the benchmark plan, let's confirm inputs: 200 prompts across short/mid/long, streaming enabled for chats, target outputs 64/128/512 tokens distribution, spike pattern 400 for 2 min every hour.

[11:46] Jenna: Got it. We'll template that into the harness. Also need dev keys and sample config - we can use a staging auth token for Hosted runs.

[11:58] Samir: Action item recap - Jenna will share harness link and run plan; Samir will send pricing and SLA; Priya to send prompts. We'll also set a follow-up in a week to review benchmark results.

[12:12] Carlos: On cost - do you have cost per token curves or effective $/1M tokens at different commit tiers?

[12:19] Samir: We'll include modeled $/M tokens for Hosted and committed Dedicated tiers in the pricing matrix. Also include amortized GPU cost for throughput.

[12:32] Priya: For long-context 8k, what p95 increase should we expect? Can you give rough factor?

[12:38] Jenna: Roughly expect 2x-5x increase in p95 depending on model and attention implementation; token/sec will drop especially for autoregressive decoders with naive attention. But our runtime uses optimized kernels that mitigate some of that. We'll provide exact numbers.

[12:56] Maya: About fallback policy - we need deterministic behavior: if Dedicated is saturated, we want fallback to lower-cost model but not to Hosted for PCI-sensitive routes. Can policies be route-level?

[13:08] Samir: Yes route-level routing policies with tags and allow-listing. You can set PCI routes to never overflow to Hosted, only to alternative Dedicated pools.

[13:22] Devon: One more - do you provide client-side SDKs that support streaming and reconnect/fallback logic?

[13:29] Jenna: Yes, we have SDKs with streaming hooks and auto-fallback logic; we can share best-practice patterns for client side to reduce p95.

[13:40] Maya: Great. Any blockers for us to run the bench? We need an NDA?

[13:45] Samir: No NDA needed for basic benchmarks; for Private/security deep dives we might need an NDA or security questionnaire. We'll send the security pack.

[13:55] (brief cross talk)

[14:02] Jenna: I'll summarize the benchmark plan in the follow-up mail: cold vs hot cache, streaming/non-streaming, concurrency vector [1, 50, 200, 400], contexts [512, 2k, 4k, 8k], quant profiles [fp16, 4-bit, 8-bit]. Output: p50/p95/p99 first-byte and full-response, tokens/sec, cost model per scenario.

[14:25] Priya: If you can also annotate which numbers are raw-inference vs end-to-end that'd help.

[14:30] Samir: We'll do that. Also attaching sample benchmark results from a previous customer for reference (link).

[14:38] Maya: Ok next steps and owners?

[14:41] Samir: Samir: pricing + SLA by 2026-06-01. Jenna: benchmark harness + initial run on Hosted with your prompts by 2026-06-04. Priya: prompt pack by 2026-05-31. Security review scheduling by 2026-06-05.

[14:58] Carlos: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[15:02] Samir: Thanks all. We'll send notes and links after the call.

[15:10] (call ends)

Notes: Link to benchmark harness: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/lynx-harness
Sample hosted result deck: https://redwood.example/decks/hosted-sample-run.pdf
Security pack link: https://redwood.example/security/pack.pdf
